messages.author: f40ceac2d3990d11
messages.subject: Print Aborts With Double Free Or Corruption Error
parts:
Print is blowing up on me for one particular model with a "double free or corruption error".  The distinguishing characterization of this model versus other simple models, where print works just fine for me, is the use of two large-ish parameter arrays being outputted.  This is happening on the git "development" branch, updated as of today. Built on Ubuntu 13.04, 64-bit, 8 cores. Will provide any additional information if needed. Thanks.

Model:

data {
  int <lower=0> N;
  real <lower=0> x[N];
  real <lower=0> tx[N];
  real <lower=0> T[N];
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0.1, upper=30> r;
  real<lower=0.1, upper=30> alpha;

  real<lower=0.1, upper=30> s;
  real<lower=0.1, upper=30> beta;

  real<lower=0, upper=1.0> lambda[N];
  real<lower=0, upper=1.0> mu[N];
}

model {
  real lm;
  real t1;
  real t2;
  real ll;
  lambda ~ gamma (r,alpha);
  mu ~ gamma (s,beta);

  for (n in 1:N) {
    lm <- lambda[n] + mu[n];
    t1 <- mu[n] * exp (- (tx[n] * lm));
    t2 <- lambda[n] * exp (- (T[n] * lm));
    ll <- x[n] * log (lambda[n]) - log (lm) + log (t1 + t2);
    increment_log_prob (ll);
  }
}


In the above N=2357, resulting in the two parameter arrays lambda[N=2357], and mu[N=2357].  When I run "print" on "samples.csv" it blows up as what appears to be exactly at the end of printing the lambda[N] array, and immediately prior to the start of printing the mu[N] array.

GDB backtrace, running simple, no other options, "print sample.csv" compiled with -g.
